title: Tensoring a local module bijection commutes with sheafification in independent universes
statement: Let C be a category, J a Grothendieck topology on C, R a presheaf of commutative rings whose underlying ring presheaf is a J-sheaf, and P,Q,N presheaves of R-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. All site, ring and module universes are independent. Suppose $f:P\to Q$ is locally injective and locally surjective for J. Assume weak sheafification of abelian-group-valued presheaves in the module universe and that J-local equivalences of such presheaves are exactly the locally bijective maps. Then the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of f tensor id_N, for the sectionwise tensor product [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product], is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 03EK (tensor product universal property) and 05V4 (tensor comparison through sheafification)

proof.text: A locally bijective map of presheaves of sets induces bijections of maps to each sheaf of sets. Given a map from its source, choose local lifts of each target section, apply the map, and glue. Local injectivity and separatedness show independence and compatibility; uniqueness proves naturality. This argument places no relation between the site and value universes.

The product of a locally bijective set-presheaf map with the identity of another presheaf is again locally bijective: use the equalizer sieve for the first coordinates for injectivity, and restrict the second coordinate along the image sieve of the first for surjectivity.

For a map g:P tensor N→H into a module sheaf, apply the first two steps to its bilinear pairing. The descended pairing on Q times N is additive and homogeneous in each variable: check the equations on the intersection of the finitely many image covering sieves, where all operands lift, and use separatedness of H. The tensor universal property gives a unique map Q tensor N→H factoring g. Injectivity follows by the same covering-sieve argument on pure tensors.

Apply the sheafification adjunction to identify the preceding bijections with precomposition by the sheafification of f tensor id_N on maps into every module sheaf. The coyoneda criterion implies that this morphism is invertible.
